title: Polynomial Simulation Budget
statement: Let $c$ be an effective machine-code scheme whose canonizer time function is polynomially bounded: there exist $C,k\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $c$'s canonizer time at input length $n$ is at most $C(n+1)^k$ for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Then there exist $A,d\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for all $m,r,t\in\mathbb{N}$ with $r\le m$ and $t\le m$, $\bigl(3r+14T_c(r)+50\bigr)(t+1)^2\le A(m+1)^d$, where $T_c$ is the canonizer time function of $c$.
hypotheses_covered: The canonizer time function of $c$ is polynomially bounded
replaced:
Let $c$ be an effective machine-code scheme, and suppose its canonizer time function
satisfies $T_c(n)\le K(n+1)^k$ for all $n\in\mathbb N$, for some $K,k\in\mathbb N$. Then
there exist $A,d\in\mathbb N$ such that, for all $m,r,t\in\mathbb N$ with $r\le m$ and
$t\le m$, $\bigl(3r+14T_c(r)+50\bigr)(t+1)^2\le A(m+1)^d$.
